Commentary.Commentary: India would be on top with the target they have set and would hope their bowlers work their magic this time around too. The chase is realistically impossible to get but if the Black Caps succeed, it will be a huge, huge achievement and would be registered in record books! Stay tuned as we come back for the third and final session on Day 4 in a short while!

New Zealand bowlers once again were taken to all parts with Mitchell Santner being the only successful bowler in terms of wickets. The visiting camp would be disappointed in themselves with their bowling performance, especially with their spinners on this turning track. Now all depends on their batsmen and how they go about the massive chase of 434.

With this declaration, it's Tea on Day 3! Session started off with two Mumbai lads out in the middle. After getting a start, Ajinkya Rahane failed to convert it into a big score and fell soon after. However his partner, Rohit Sharma stayed unbeaten on a well played 68. After Rahane fell, India sent in Ravindra Jadeja to attack and he did full justice to his role scoring a quick unbeaten 50.

India have set a target of 434 to New Zealand! What a performance by the Indian batsmen. Except the skipper, each and ever batsman got a start for themselves. Four of them went on to make their respective half-centuries and contributed for this massive 3rd innings total. New Zealand bowlers never did trouble the Indian batsmen much and let the game slip far from their reach.

The players are out in the middle and Murali Vijay and Cheteshwar Pujara will look to swell the lead even more. Will the New Zealand bowlers break the dominant partnership and give themselves a chance to fight back? Let's find out! Ish Sodhi to start the proceedings today!

Hello and a warm welcome to Day 4 of the first Test between India and New Zealand. The home side are well and truly in the driver's seat with a healthy 215-run lead and it would require something more than extraordinary for the Kiwis to pave their way back into the match. It's a touch overcast right now and let's hope the weather clears out and it becomes bright and sunny like yesterday to treat us with loads of excitement and drama.
... DAY 4, SESSION 1 ...

The Kiwis face an uphill task to come back from here and if they are successful in doing it, it would be nothing less than a miracle. Join us tomorrow at 0915 IST and hopefully the sun would shine bright and we will witness another enthralling day of cricket. Till then, goodbye and take care!

Earlier in the day, the home side bowled really well to wrap up the tourists for 262 and notched up a lead of 56. They were quite clinical throughout the day and it has hands down belonged to them. The highlight of the day was Jadeja taking his fifth fifer in Tests. India are in a really strong position now. They would look to come out tomorrow and bat aggressively to stretch their 215-run lead even more to bat New Zealand out of the game.

A session that has been dominated thoroughly by the Indians as Pujara and Vijay have extended the lead to 215 without breaking a sweat! They have played positive cricket by playing the ball on its merit and never let the Kiwi spinners settle down. They are amidst an unbroken century stand and are driving the visiting side out of the contest. Neil Wagner tried hard and employed the short ball strategy but both of them played him nonchalantly as he failed to execute his plan properly. The other bowlers also tried their best but they couldn't bother the confident duo.

The Indian openers started on a high, with KL Rahul being the aggressor and Murali Vijay playing out his patient game. They were about to see off this session without any setback and just then they lost Rahul. The NZ spinners bowled well too, getting the odd ball to bounce and turn. India now lead by 108 runs. Let's see what the last session has in it for us. Stay tuned as we will be back in short while!

A near perfect session for India, it would have been perfect if they hadn't lost the wicket at the stroke of Tea. nevertheless, they won it fair and square. They started the session on a high with their spin duo of Ravichandran Ashwin and Ravindra Jadeja doing the damage and bowling out the Kiwis for 262, giving a 56-run lead for India.
